v. When Normal distribution is shown on a graph paper, it gives a bell-shaped curve called Normal curve which is generally taken as a standard for comparison.

4.2.1 Definition of Normal probability distribution

A random variable X is said to follow a Normal distribution if its probability density function is

$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2},\quad -\infty\le X\le\infty,\ -\infty\le\mu\le\infty,\ 0\le\sigma\le\infty$

Where

X = Normal random variable.

f(x) = The height of the curve corresponding to a given value of X.

μ = mean of Normal distribution.

σ = standard deviation of Normal distribution

π = a constant approximately equal to \frac{22}{7}=3.1429

e = a constant approximately equal to 2.7183.

This distribution has two parameters, μ and \sigma^2. Normal distribution is simply written as X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2).

4.2.2 Properties of Normal distribution

i) The total probability within its range −∞ to +∞ is always equal to one i.e.

$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2}dx=1$

ii) The Normal distribution is symmetrical about the mean and is a bell-shaped.

iii) Mean = Median = Mode.

iv) The Normal curve is unimodal.

v) The first and third quartiles are equidistant from the centre, or Mean μ.

vi) Q.D=\frac{2}{3}\sigma and M.D=\frac{4}{5}\sigma

vii) All odd order moments about mean i.e. \mu_1,\mu_3,\ldots are zero.

viii) Measures of skewness, \beta_1=0 or \gamma_1=0

ix) Measures of kurtosis, \beta_2=3 or \gamma_2=0

x) For Normal distribution, out of the total observation, 68.3 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm\sigma), 95.4 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm 2\sigma) and 99.7 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm 3\sigma). Graphically this statement is shown as

4.2.3 Standard normal variable

Normal random variable X is transformed by subtracting its mean from it and the difference is divided by its standard deviation and is called standard Normal variable, usually denoted by Z, that is

$Z=\frac{X-\mu}{\sigma}$

Possible values of Z are also form −∞ to +∞.

σ = نارمل تقسیم کا معیاری انحراف

π = ایک مستقل جو تقریباً \frac{22}{7}=3.1429 کے برابر ہے

e = ایک مستقل جو تقریباً 2.7183 کے برابر ہے۔

اس تقسیم کے دو پیرامیٹر μ اور \sigma^2 ہیں۔ نارمل تقسیم کو سادہ طور پر X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2) لکھا جاتا ہے۔

4.2.2 نارمل تقسیم کی خصوصیات

i) اس کی حد −∞ سے +∞ کے اندر کل احتمال ہمیشہ ایک کے برابر ہوتا ہے یعنی

$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2}dx=1$

ii) نارمل تقسیم اوسط کے گرد متشاکل اور گھنٹی نما ہوتی ہے۔

iii) اوسط = وسطانیہ = عادہ۔

iv) نارمل منحنی یک عادی (unimodal) ہوتی ہے۔

v) پہلا اور تیسرا ربعیہ مرکز یعنی اوسط μ سے برابر فاصلے پر ہوتے ہیں۔

vi) Q.D=\frac{2}{3}\sigma اور M.D=\frac{4}{5}\sigma

vii) اوسط کے گرد تمام طاق درجے کے معیارِ اثر (moments) یعنی \mu_1,\mu_3,\ldots صفر ہوتے ہیں۔

viii) چولاؤ (skewness) کی پیمائش، \beta_1=0 یا \gamma_1=0

ix) نوک داری (kurtosis) کی پیمائش، \beta_2=3 یا \gamma_2=0

x) نارمل تقسیم میں کل مشاہدات میں سے 68.3 % حدود (\mu\pm\sigma) کے اندر، 95.4 % حدود (\mu\pm 2\sigma) کے اندر اور 99.7 % حدود (\mu\pm 3\sigma) کے اندر ہوتے ہیں۔ ترسیمی طور پر یہ بیان یوں دکھایا جاتا ہے

4.2.3 معیاری نارمل متغیر

نارمل تصادفی متغیر X میں سے اس کا اوسط تفریق کر کے اور فرق کو اس کے معیاری انحراف پر تقسیم کر کے تبدیل کیا جاتا ہے، اسے معیاری نارمل متغیر کہتے ہیں اور عموماً Z سے ظاہر کرتے ہیں، یعنی

$Z=\frac{X-\mu}{\sigma}$

Z کی ممکنہ قیمتیں بھی −∞ سے +∞ تک ہیں۔

v. When Normal distribution is shown on a graph paper, it gives a bell-shaped curve called Normal curve which is generally taken as a standard for comparison.

4.2.1 Definition of Normal probability distribution

A random variable X is said to follow a Normal distribution if its probability density function is

$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2},\quad -\infty\le X\le\infty,\ -\infty\le\mu\le\infty,\ 0\le\sigma\le\infty$

Where

X = Normal random variable.

f(x) = The height of the curve corresponding to a given value of X.

μ = mean of Normal distribution.

σ = standard deviation of Normal distribution

π = a constant approximately equal to \frac{22}{7}=3.1429

e = a constant approximately equal to 2.7183.

This distribution has two parameters, μ and \sigma^2. Normal distribution is simply written as X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2).

4.2.2 Properties of Normal distribution

i) The total probability within its range −∞ to +∞ is always equal to one i.e.

$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2}dx=1$

ii) The Normal distribution is symmetrical about the mean and is a bell-shaped.

iii) Mean = Median = Mode.

iv) The Normal curve is unimodal.

v) The first and third quartiles are equidistant from the centre, or Mean μ.

vi) Q.D=\frac{2}{3}\sigma and M.D=\frac{4}{5}\sigma

vii) All odd order moments about mean i.e. \mu_1,\mu_3,\ldots are zero.

viii) Measures of skewness, \beta_1=0 or \gamma_1=0

ix) Measures of kurtosis, \beta_2=3 or \gamma_2=0

x) For Normal distribution, out of the total observation, 68.3 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm\sigma), 95.4 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm 2\sigma) and 99.7 % lies within the limits (\mu\pm 3\sigma). Graphically this statement is shown as

4.2.3 Standard normal variable

Normal random variable X is transformed by subtracting its mean from it and the difference is divided by its standard deviation and is called standard Normal variable, usually denoted by Z, that is

$Z=\frac{X-\mu}{\sigma}$

Possible values of Z are also form −∞ to +∞.
